verses.1: By the rivers of Babylon we sat down and wept when we remembered Zion.
verses.2: On the willows there we hung our lyres.
verses.3: For there our captors asked us for songs, and our tormentors demanded a joyous melody: "Sing for us a song of Zion!"
verses.4: How can we sing the LORD's song in a foreign land?
verses.5: If I forget you, Jerusalem, may my right hand forget its skill.
verses.6: If I do not remember you, may my tongue cling to the roof of my mouth—if I do not place Jerusalem above all my joys.
verses.7: Remember, LORD, the children of Edom, the day Jerusalem fell, the cry: "Tear it down! Tear it down! Even to its foundations!"
verses.8: O daughter of Babylon, doomed to destruction, blessed is the one who repays you for what you have done to us—
verses.9: blessed is the one who seizes your infants and dashes them against the rock.

notes:
Notes  
- v. 9: The final line is deliberately shocking and graphic, reflecting the intensity of the psalmist's grief and desire for retribution. The translation follows the Hebrew phrasing, which is direct and unambiguous.
raw:
[1] By the rivers of Babylon we sat down and wept when we remembered Zion.  
[2] On the willows there we hung our lyres.  
[3] For there our captors asked us for songs, and our tormentors demanded a joyous melody: "Sing for us a song of Zion!"  
[4] How can we sing the LORD's song in a foreign land?  
[5] If I forget you, Jerusalem, may my right hand forget its skill.  
[6] If I do not remember you, may my tongue cling to the roof of my mouth—if I do not place Jerusalem above all my joys.  
[7] Remember, LORD, the children of Edom, the day Jerusalem fell, the cry: "Tear it down! Tear it down! Even to its foundations!"  
[8] O daughter of Babylon, doomed to destruction, blessed is the one who repays you for what you have done to us—  
[9] blessed is the one who seizes your infants and dashes them against the rock.  
---

- v. 9: The final line is deliberately shocking and graphic, reflecting the intensity of the psalmist's grief and desire for retribution. The translation follows the Hebrew phrasing, which is direct and unambiguous.
